title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
summary: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration. Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an…
llm_summary: The U.S. Southwest’s hydropower output fell to a record low this summer, producing about 28 % less electricity from April through August than the ten‑year average, according to the Energy Information Administration. Drought‑driven drops in reservoir levels have limited the water flow through dam‑based turbines, curbing generation when the grid needs it most. This shortfall highlights how climate‑induced water scarcity can directly impact renewable‑energy
